top_jobs.job: When our best ad is getting more expensive and the media buyer needs new words by Friday, help me get copy built from what buyers say, for the buyers who convert best, that wins on cost per purchase and not on clicks, so I launch fresh ads without paying more for each sale
top_jobs.metric: cost per purchase by copy set, 7 day click, first 14 days live

top_jobs.job: When new ads are due to go live tomorrow and I do not know if a line breaks Meta's rules or promises something we cannot back, help me check every claim, quote and boast first and cut drafts to our voice, so I launch without a rejection and stop rewriting every line myself
top_jobs.metric: ads rejected per 100 launched, and share of drafts approved without a rewrite

top_jobs.job: When the ad promises one thing and the page it sends to says another, or people visit and do not buy, help me find which live ads no longer match their page and which doubt costs the most sales, so I stop paying for clicks that land on the wrong message
top_jobs.metric: conversion rate of paid sessions on the top 10 ads' landing pages

top_jobs.job: When retargeting shows the same ad again and new ads only speak to people who already know us, help me write a different argument for each awareness level and each buying moment, so I win back the doubters and reach buyers our normal ads miss
top_jobs.metric: cost per new customer by awareness level of the copy

top_jobs.job: When a proven ad starts to cost 30 percent more per sale and the buyer wants to cut the price, help me change the headline, the price line or the offer in the right order and give reasons to buy that are not a discount, so I save the ad without giving away margin
top_jobs.metric: gross profit per order on ads with refreshed copy

jobs.job: Split every ad we ran in 12 months into avatar, pain point, promise, proof and CTA, rank each avatar and pain pair by spend and cost per purchase, and list the pairs no ad speaks to
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then every new ad within a day of launch

inputs.need: 12 months of ad copy, headlines and results at ad level
up to 4 avatars and their pain points
landing page text per ad URL
a person to check 20 splits a week

steps: Pull primary text, headline, description and URL for every ad with spend
Tag each ad with one avatar, one pain point, the promise, the proof type and the CTA
Check 20 at random by hand and fix the avatar and pain definitions that are wrong
Compute in code per pair: ads, spend, purchases, cost per purchase, share of new customers
Build a grid of avatars by pains; mark cells with spend, cells that win, and empty cells
jobs.output: an avatar by pain grid with spend, cost per purchase and empty cells marked
jobs.next: feeds 10-04 (copy per segment) and 10-05 (Friday copy batch)

watch.metric: share of spend on the 3 cheapest avatar and pain pairs

jobs.drives: cost per new customer

jobs.job: Mine our reviews and 3 rivals' Amazon and site reviews for what buyers love, hate and wish for, and build a bank of the 20 most used phrases per theme with counts
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then on the 1st of each month

inputs.need: all our reviews with text, rating and product
rivals' reviews from Amazon and their sites, 3 rivals
inputs.from: a review export tool or a paid data source

inputs.need: our Amazon reviews and questions, when we sell there
return reasons

steps: Pull 5 star and 1 star reviews first, then the rest
Group sentences into themes: loved, hated, wished for, surprised by, used instead
Count each theme per brand and keep the exact phrases, with source
Mark where rivals fail most (1 star themes) and we are praised for the same thing
Write the top 20 phrases per theme into the language bank; forum quotes are never testimonials
jobs.output: a language bank: themes with counts for us and each rival, and 20 verbatim phrases per theme

watch.metric: click rate and cost per purchase of ads using bank phrases vs not

jobs.drives: cost per purchase on new copy

jobs.job: Move proven words between channels each month: turn the top 20 Google search terms, Search Console queries and Amazon questions into 10 Meta hooks, and turn the 5 best Meta hooks into Google headlines and article titles
jobs.trigger: on the 1st of each month

inputs.need: Google Ads search terms with purchases, 90 days
Search Console queries with clicks and position
Amazon questions and review phrases
site search terms
Meta hooks with cost per purchase

steps: List the 20 search terms with the most purchases and the 20 fastest rising queries
Add the 10 most asked Amazon questions and site searches
Rewrite 10 of them as Meta hooks in the searcher's words, e.g. a query 'socks that do not slip' becomes the first line
Take the 5 Meta hooks with the lowest cost per purchase and write 3 Google headlines each within 30 characters
Send 3 article titles built from winning hooks and rising queries to 17-seo
Tag each line with its source so its result is traced back
jobs.output: a monthly bridge sheet: 10 Meta hooks from search, 15 Google headlines from Meta, 3 article titles

watch.metric: cost per purchase of search-sourced Meta hooks vs account median

jobs.drives: cost per new customer across Meta and Google

jobs.job: Write 3 copy sets for each of the 2 cheapest segments by age, gender and placement, using their pain and their words, so the ad reads as if it were written for them
jobs.trigger: every other Monday, and before each launch slot

inputs.need: purchases and cost per new customer by age, gender and placement, 28 days
avatar and pain grid
language bank
placement text limits and safe zones

steps: Pick the 2 cells with the lowest cost per new customer and at least 30 purchases, e.g. women 35 to 44 on Reels
Match each cell to the avatar that most often buys there, from order and survey data
Write 3 sets per cell: primary text, headline, on-screen line, sized to that placement
Use the words that cell uses in reviews; drop lines that only fit the other cell
Hand the sets to the media buyer with the cell each is for
jobs.output: 6 copy sets, each labelled with the segment and placement it is written for
jobs.next: feeds 11-12 (ad sets for the best segment)

watch.metric: cost per purchase in the target segment vs generic copy

jobs.drives: cost per new customer

jobs.job: Write the Friday copy batch: 10 headline candidates for each chosen avatar and pain pair, cut to 3 truly different angles, each with a written reason and a pass line
jobs.trigger: every Wednesday for a Friday launch slot, and when the top ad's cost per purchase rises 15 percent

inputs.need: the pair to write for
winner cards from creative
language bank and objection ladder
ad copy playbook v1.2 and ad copy ideas

steps: Write the buying question: what the reader believes now and what they must believe to buy
Write 10 headlines, each with a true specific: a number, a time, a count or a price
Cut to 3 that differ in angle, not synonyms; name the angle of each
Write the primary text for each: first line under 14 words, one idea, one proof
Write the reason each might win and the cost per purchase that counts as a pass
Run 10-09 on the 3 before they go to the media buyer
jobs.output: 3 copy sets with angle names, reasons and pass lines, ready for Friday

watch.metric: cost per purchase by copy set, 7 day click

jobs.drives: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.job: Refresh a tiring winner's words without losing its appeal: keep the promise and the proof, and change only the first line, the headline and the form (list, story or question)
jobs.trigger: when fatigue-watch labels a winner worn out

inputs.need: the worn out ad and its split into promise, proof and CTA
wear label and dates
voice rules

steps: Write the promise and proof of the winner in one line each; these do not change
Write 3 new forms: a numbered list, a short customer story with a turn, a question the buyer asks
Write 3 new first lines and 3 new headlines per form
Pick 3 full sets and run them through 10-09
Launch beside the old ad, not in place of it
jobs.output: 3 refreshed copy sets on the same promise, ready to launch

watch.metric: cost per purchase of refreshed sets vs the old ad's last 7 days

jobs.drives: life of a winning message in weeks

jobs.job: Check every line in tomorrow's ads against the claims shelf and Meta's rules: health and before and after claims, personal attributes, fake scarcity, review quotes and guarantees, and return a pass, fix or block per line
jobs.trigger: before every launch, the day before

inputs.need: the ads due tomorrow with all text and on-screen text
allowed claims with proof files, and forbidden claims
Meta ad rules for the category, written as checks
review quotes with permission status

steps: Split each ad into single lines, including on-screen text and captions
Match each line to an allowed claim and its proof file; lines with no match go to fix
Flag rule risks: 'you' plus a body or money problem, before and after, cures, invented scarcity
Check every quote is real, permitted and not changed in meaning
Write a passing rewrite for each fix; block lines with no proof
A person signs the block list before launch
jobs.output: a line by line check with pass, fix (and the rewrite) or block, signed before launch

watch.metric: ads rejected per 100 launched

jobs.drives: days of delivery lost to rejections, and account health

jobs.job: Swap every boast in live and draft copy (best, premium, amazing, world class) for a number, a rating or a test result we can back, and list the boasts with no proof to replace
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then on every draft batch

inputs.need: live ad copy and product page copy
proof per product: ratings, review counts, tests, specs
banned words

steps: Scan all lines for a list of 40 boast words and banned words
For each hit, find a true specific from the products shelf, e.g. '4.8 stars from 12,000 reviews'
Rewrite the line with the specific; never invent a number
List boasts with no proof to the founder as proof to find or lines to drop
jobs.output: a swap list of boasts to specifics, and a short list of claims that need proof
jobs.next: feeds 10-09 (voice check) and the claims shelf

watch.metric: share of live lines with a specific number or proof

jobs.drives: click rate and cost per purchase

jobs.job: Score each batch of freelancer or AI drafts in code for reading level, sentence length, banned words and voice rules, and cut 20 drafts to the 5 worth the founder's time
jobs.trigger: when a batch of drafts arrives

inputs.need: the drafts
voice rules, 20 liked and 20 disliked examples
readability and banned word checks
the founder's past ratings of copy

steps: Score reading level in code; fail anything above grade 8
Fail sentences over 20 words, banned words, em dashes and vague words
Compare each draft with liked and disliked examples and give a voice score
Rank by score and by how different the angle is from the others
Send the top 5 with one line on why each passed; log the founder's pick to the ratings
jobs.output: 5 drafts that pass voice and reading checks, with scores, from a batch of 20
jobs.next: feeds 10-07 (claim check) and the voice shelf ratings

watch.metric: share of drafts the founder approves without a rewrite

jobs.drives: founder hours spent on copy per week

jobs.job: Fix a rejected ad within the hour: find the words that triggered it, write 3 rewrites that keep the angle and pass, and log the rule so it is checked next time
jobs.trigger: when Meta rejects an ad or warns the account

inputs.need: rejection notice and the rejected ad
past rejections and the rewrites that passed
allowed claims

steps: Read the policy named in the notice and mark the lines and images that fit it
Write 3 rewrites that keep the angle and drop the trigger
Run them through 10-07
The media buyer submits one; request review only if the ad was clearly within the rules
Add the trigger and the passing line to the rejection log
jobs.output: 3 passing rewrites and a new line in the rejection log

watch.metric: hours from rejection to the ad running again

jobs.drives: days of delivery lost and account warnings

jobs.job: Score the top 10 ads by spend for match with their landing page on promise, offer, picture and awareness level, and rewrite the page headline of the worst 3 to mirror the ad within a day
jobs.trigger: every Monday, and after any page or offer change

inputs.need: top 10 ads with URL, copy and media
landing page text and a screenshot per URL
paid sessions and conversion by landing page and ad
awareness level per ad

steps: For each ad, write its promise, offer and awareness level in one line each
Read the top of the landing page as a phone user sees it and write the same 3
Score 0 to 3: promise matches, offer matches, picture matches the ad
For the 3 lowest scores, write a new headline and sub line that repeat the ad's promise
Send the change to 07-landing-pages-cro and compare conversion 14 days before and after
jobs.output: a match score for the top 10 ads and 3 page headline rewrites

watch.metric: conversion rate of paid sessions on the 3 fixed pages

jobs.drives: cost per purchase on those ads

jobs.job: When a sale ends or a product sells out, list every live ad, email, page line and listing that still says it, and hand over the fixes before midnight
jobs.trigger: on each sale end date and each sellout

inputs.need: live ads with text
live flows and scheduled campaigns
offer end dates and stock state
site crawl text

steps: Take the ended offer or the sold out product name
Search every live line for the code, the percent, the product name and 'ends'
List each hit with where it runs and who owns it
Write the replacement line for each; pausing ads stays with the media buyer
Recheck the next morning that no hit is still live
jobs.output: a sweep list of stale lines with owners and replacement lines, rechecked next day
jobs.next: feeds 11-18 (move spend off sold out products)

watch.metric: live lines still naming an ended offer or sold out product

jobs.drives: tickets about wrong prices and trust

jobs.job: List every question buyers ask per hero product from tickets, Amazon questions, reviews and site search, mark where each is answered, and write the answer line for the 3 unanswered doubts that cost the most sales
jobs.trigger: once a month per hero product, and when a product page's add to cart rate drops

inputs.need: tickets and chats tagged by product, 6 months
Amazon questions per product
product page, FAQ and ad text
scroll depth on the product page

steps: Pull every question and group into 15 doubts: fit, size, wash, ship time, returns, price, and so on
Count each doubt and mark if it is answered on the page, in the FAQ, in ads, in email
Rank blank cells by count times the product's traffic
Write a short true answer for the top 3, placed where Clarity shows buyers still read
Add the top doubt's answer as a line in one retargeting ad
jobs.output: a doubt by channel matrix per product and 3 answer lines placed on page and in one ad

watch.metric: add to cart rate on the product page

jobs.drives: product page conversion and tickets per 100 orders

jobs.job: Carry each winning ad line to the product page, the welcome email and the listing within a week, and log where it now runs
jobs.trigger: when a copy test is read as a win

inputs.need: the winning line and its test result
the page, email and listing where the product is sold
Amazon listing access, when they sell there

steps: Write the line as a page headline, an email subject and first line, and a listing bullet
Check each fits the place's length limit and awareness level
Send each to its owner with the test result as the reason
Log where the line runs in the messaging shelf with the date
jobs.output: one proven line live on page, email and listing, logged in the messaging shelf

watch.metric: conversion rate on the product page and welcome email click rate

jobs.drives: revenue per visitor

jobs.job: Tag all ad copy by awareness level, and for the thinnest level write 3 copy sets at the right story depth: long native text for unaware, the problem named for problem aware, the method for solution aware
jobs.trigger: every other Monday, after the awareness heat map updates

inputs.need: heat map with the gap line
problem words and moments from buyers
the story bank
top of funnel copy ideas

steps: Read the gap level from the heat map, e.g. problem aware at 6 percent of spend
Write the buyer's state at that level in one line: what they know and do not know
Write 3 sets: open on the problem, not the product; name the product only after the reason
For unaware, write 150 to 300 words of native text that reads like a post, not an ad
Point each set to a page at the same level, not straight to checkout
jobs.output: 3 copy sets at the gap level, each with its matching landing page
jobs.next: feeds 11-11 (top of funnel budget) and 09-12 (visual briefs)

watch.metric: new customer share of purchases from these sets

jobs.drives: new customers per week

jobs.job: Write one retargeting ad per top objection for people who visited in the last 30 days and did not buy, each with a different argument and its proof, never the same ad again
jobs.trigger: once a month, and when retargeting frequency passes 4

inputs.need: objection ladder ranked by sales lost
top unanswered doubts per product
proof per product: reviews, tests, guarantee
retargeting ad sets and their frequency

steps: Take the top 3 objections, e.g. 'will it fit', 'is it worth the price', 'can I return it'
Write one ad per objection: name it, answer it, show the proof
Use a different picture from the cold ad the visitor already saw
Keep the same argument across the follow-up ads in the sequence
Read each by cost per purchase on 7 day click, not by view-through
jobs.output: 3 retargeting ads, one per objection, with proof
jobs.next: feeds 11-10 (retargeting slice of the funnel mix)

watch.metric: cost per purchase in retargeting ad sets

jobs.drives: conversion of site visitors who did not buy

jobs.job: Write copy for each buying moment our ads miss, starting with gift buyers 3 weeks before a gifting date: who it is for, why it is a safe gift, when it arrives, how returns work
jobs.trigger: quarterly from the moments table, and 3 weeks before each gifting date

inputs.need: the moments table with counts
gifting dates and ship cut-offs
gift options: wrap, notes, gift returns
share of orders shipped to a different address

steps: Pick the moment no live ad speaks to that has the most buyers
Write who buys, for whom, and the doubt at that moment
Write 3 sets; for gifts, answer 'will they like it' and 'will it arrive in time' with dates
Add the order-by date in digits for gifting sets
Send each set to the media buyer with its start and stop date
jobs.output: 3 copy sets per moment, with start and stop dates for seasonal ones

watch.metric: orders shipped to a different address than billing

jobs.drives: revenue in gifting weeks

jobs.job: When a proven ad's cost per purchase rises 30 percent, test in order: a new headline first, then a new price line, then a new offer, one at a time, before anyone cuts the price
jobs.trigger: when a winner's cost per purchase is up 30 percent for 7 days

inputs.need: the ad's daily results for 28 days
margin per product and the discount floor
wear label

steps: Rule out wear first: if hook rate has fallen, send it to 09-09 instead
Step 1: test 3 new headlines on the same ad for 7 days
Step 2, only if step 1 fails: restate price as cost per day or per use, or add a bundle saving line
Step 3, only if step 2 fails: propose an offer inside the discount floor, for founder sign-off
Log each step's result in the ledger
jobs.output: a 3 step rescue test with a result at each step, and a price cut only as the last resort

watch.metric: cost per purchase on the rescued ad

jobs.drives: gross profit per order

jobs.job: Turn each approved sale or bundle into one offer line (what, how much, until when) and check it against the live code, the price and the end date in the store before it ships
jobs.trigger: when an offer is approved, 7 days before it starts

inputs.need: the approved offer with rules
discount codes, prices and product eligibility
the offer calendar

steps: Write the offer as one line with digits: '20 percent off 3 packs, ends Sunday 11:59 pm ET'
Check the code exists, applies to the right products and ends at the stated time
Write the ad, email and page versions of the same line
Put the end date into the sweep list for 10-12
jobs.output: one checked offer line in 3 versions, with the end date scheduled for the sweep

watch.metric: tickets about a wrong price or code in the sale week

jobs.drives: sale revenue and trust

jobs.job: Write 5 reasons to buy each hero product that are not a discount (proof, fit, method, guarantee, cost per use) and test the best 2 against the current discount ad
jobs.trigger: once a quarter, and when discount orders pass 50 percent of orders

inputs.need: share of orders with a discount code and margin per order
praise themes and phrases
product proof and guarantee terms

steps: Compute in code the share of orders and gross profit that came with a code
Write 5 reasons from praise themes and proof, e.g. 'lasts 2 years of weekly wear'
Pick 2 with the most review mentions
Run each as an ad with no code against the current discount ad, same audience and budget
Compare gross profit per 1,000 impressions, not just cost per purchase
jobs.output: 5 no discount reasons per hero product and a test of the top 2 against the discount ad

watch.metric: share of orders with a discount code

jobs.drives: gross profit per order

new_enablers.name: Claim and live line check
new_enablers.what: Keeps an index of every live line in ads, emails, pages and listings with its claim, proof file, offer and end date. Checks new lines against the claims shelf, platform ad rules and a log of past rejections, and sweeps for stale offers and sold out products.
inputs: platform ad rules written as checks
live ads, emails, pages and listings
past rejections and the rewrites that passed
powers: no launch with an unproven claim
no stale sale lines after midnight

new_enablers.name: Voice and readability check
new_enablers.what: Scores any draft in code for reading level, sentence length, banned words, boasts and em dashes, and compares it with the founder's liked and disliked examples. Ranks a batch so the founder reads only the best.
powers: same voice from any writer or AI tool
